- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 1–2 days.
- If sentiment is low or neutral (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 3–5% downward adjustment for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model exhibits persistent bias; apply a 3–5% downward correction to all forecasts unless sentiment shifts to positive.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0, model often fails to adjust downward; if sentiment is 1.0 and price is falling, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overconfidence bias.
